definitions.gloss: thoroughly; from beginning to end; completely; through and through
definitions.explanation: An emphatic expression meaning to do something consistently and completely, without wavering or compromising, from start to finish.

examples.japanese: {徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}{反対|はんたい}した。
{彼|かれ}は{徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}{自分|じぶん}の{意見|いけん}を{貫|つらぬ}いた。
examples.english: He stuck to his opinion through and through.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}シリアスな{作品|さくひん}で、{笑|わら}えるシーンは{一|ひと}つもなかった。
examples.english: This movie was serious through and through, without a single funny scene.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) meaning "piercing head, piercing tail" — thorough from the very beginning ({頭|あたま}) to the very end ({尾|お}). {徹|てつ} means to penetrate or go through completely.

USAGE:
A formal, emphatic adverb used primarily in written language and formal speech. Emphasizes unwavering consistency.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}{反対|はんたい}する (to oppose completely)
- {徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}{貫|つらぬ}く (to maintain consistently)
- {徹頭徹尾|てっとうてつび}{一貫|いっかん}している (to be consistent throughout)
